name: Architecture / Design Firm
description: Architecture and design firm organized around the studio model with a structured licensure track. Built on a hierarchy from Principals/Partners through Project Architects, Architectural Designers, and Interns/Drafters. Studios specialize by sector (residential, commercial, institutional, healthcare, etc.) with shared services in marketing, finance, and operations. Professionals progress through a defined track from intern through licensed architect to principal.

org_structure.overview: Architecture firms typically follow a studio model where teams specialize in building types or sectors. The organization is led by Principals or Partners who own the firm and set strategic direction. Project Architects lead the design and documentation of individual projects supported by Architectural Designers and Interns. The profession has a structured licensure track: graduates complete the Architectural Experience Program (AXP), pass the Architect Registration Examination (ARE), and become licensed architects. Many firms offer multiple disciplines under one roof including architecture, interior design, landscape architecture, urban planning, and sometimes structural engineering. Studios operate semi-autonomously within the firm, sharing administrative services and cross-staffing as needed.

departments.name: Firm Leadership / Principals
departments.description: Owners and senior leaders who set firm vision, manage business performance, and maintain client relationships. Principals are typically licensed architects who have advanced through the ranks or founded the firm.

roles.title: Principal / Partner
roles.description: Owner of the firm; responsible for firm strategy, financial performance, major client relationships, design vision, and culture. Often serves as the 'name' on the door.

roles.title: Managing Principal
roles.description: Senior principal responsible for firm operations; manages other principals, firm finances, strategic planning, and day-to-day business leadership.

roles.title: Studio Director
roles.description: Principal or senior associate leading a specific studio (e.g., Healthcare, Commercial, Education); responsible for studio P&L, staff, project delivery, and business development within the sector.

departments.name: Project Architecture Teams
departments.description: The core project delivery teams within each studio. Licensed architects lead projects, with designers and interns supporting design development, construction documents, and construction administration.

roles.title: Project Architect
roles.description: Licensed architect leading project delivery: manages design development, construction documents, code compliance, consultant coordination, and construction administration.

roles.title: Senior Architectural Designer
roles.description: Experienced designer contributing to concept design, schematic design, design development, and visualization. May be on licensure track or a specialist designer.

roles.title: Architectural Designer / Drafter
roles.description: Produces architectural drawings, 3D models, renderings, and technical documentation under the supervision of a licensed architect. Developing toward licensure.

roles.title: Intern Architect / Architectural Associate
roles.description: Recent graduate completing AXP hours toward licensure; performs drafting, modeling, research, code analysis, and basic design tasks under supervision.

roles.title: BIM / Revit Specialist
roles.description: Specialist in Building Information Modeling software; manages model standards, family creation, clash detection, and BIM execution plans.

roles.title: Specifications Writer
roles.description: Specializes in writing project specifications: material selections, performance criteria, quality standards, and construction administration requirements.

departments.name: Design Studios
departments.description: Sector-focused semi-autonomous teams that specialize in specific building types: commercial, residential, healthcare, education, institutional, interior design, landscape, urban planning. Each studio has a director and dedicated project teams.

roles.title: Commercial / Office Studio
roles.description: Specializes in commercial office buildings, mixed-use developments, corporate campuses, and workplace design.

roles.title: Residential Studio
roles.description: Specializes in single-family, multi-family, condominium, and luxury residential design.

roles.title: Healthcare Studio
roles.description: Specializes in hospitals, clinics, medical offices, and healthcare facilities with expertise in complex regulatory and operational requirements.

roles.title: Education / Institutional Studio
roles.description: Specializes in K-12 schools, universities, libraries, museums, and public institutional buildings.

roles.title: Interior Design Studio
roles.description: Specializes in interior architecture, space planning, finishes selection, FF&E, and workplace strategy for interior environments.

roles.title: Urban Design / Planning Studio
roles.description: Specializes in master planning, urban design, zoning analysis, land use planning, and community development projects.

departments.name: Sustainability & Technical Specialists
departments.description: Cross-studio experts who provide specialized technical knowledge to all projects: sustainable design, building performance, structural engineering, and building envelope design.

roles.title: Sustainability Director
roles.description: Leads sustainable design initiatives: LEED certification, energy modeling, net-zero design, material health, and firm sustainability strategy.

roles.title: Building Performance Analyst
roles.description: Performs energy modeling, daylight analysis, thermal comfort studies, and building performance simulations to optimize design.

roles.title: Structural Engineer (In-House)
roles.description: Provides in-house structural engineering for projects; coordinates with architectural teams on structural systems design and documentation.

roles.title: Landscape Architect
roles.description: Designs site landscapes, hardscapes, planting plans, green infrastructure, and outdoor spaces in coordination with architectural teams.

departments.name: Business Development & Marketing
departments.description: Drives firm growth through proposal development, client relationships, industry events, and brand management. In architecture, business development is heavily relationship-driven and often led by principals with marketer support.

roles.title: Marketing Director / BD Manager
roles.description: Leads business development and marketing: RFP responses, proposal strategy, client relationship management, industry events, and firm brand.

roles.title: Proposal Coordinator / Marketer
roles.description: Coordinates proposal responses, prepares marketing collateral, maintains project photography, manages awards submissions, and supports BD efforts.

roles.title: Client Relationship Manager
roles.description: Develops and maintains relationships with key clients, tracks client satisfaction, identifies follow-on opportunities, and manages CRM systems.

roles.title: Communications / PR Coordinator
roles.description: Manages firm website, social media, press releases, publications, and internal communications.

departments.name: Firm Operations & Support
departments.description: Shared services that support all studios: finance/accounting, HR, IT, and office management. Handle the business side so studio teams can focus on project delivery.

roles.title: Finance / Accounting Manager
roles.description: Manges firm financials: billing, accounts receivable, project profitability tracking, payroll, and financial reporting.

roles.title: Project Accountant
roles.description: Tracks project budgets, invoices, billable hours, consultant payments, and revenue recognition for individual projects.

roles.title: HR Manager
roles.description: Manges recruitment, professional development, performance reviews, benefits administration, and licensure support programs.

roles.title: IT / Technology Manager
roles.description: Manges IT infrastructure, BIM/Revit server management, software licenses, file sharing systems, and technology support.

roles.title: Office Manager / Administrator
roles.description: Manges office operations: reception, supplies, mailing, vendor relationships, and general administrative support.

roles.title: Librarian / Resource Specialist
roles.description: Maintains material sample library, product literature, digital resources, and specification reference materials for design teams.

key_relationships: Project Architect reports to the Studio Director but works closely with the Principal-in-Charge on design vision, client communication, and project financials.
Intern Architect is directly supervised by a licensed Project Architect who signs off on AXP experience hours required for licensure.
Studio Directors collaborate on cross-studio staffing when projects require specialized expertise from multiple sectors.
Marketing Director works with each Studio Director and Principal to develop sector-specific proposals and client targeting strategies.
Sustainability Director collaborates with all studios to incorporate sustainable design strategies into every project phase.
BIM/Revit Specialist supports all studios and project teams with model management and technology training.
Project Accountant partners with each Project Architect to track project profitability, billing milestones, and change order impact.
HR Manager coordinates with Studio Directors on recruitment needs, intern development programs, and licensure support.
Specifications Writer coordinates with Project Architects and consultants to ensure construction documents accurately reflect design intent.
